The reaction search explicitly decoded the latter three neutral components as THF, DMF, and the dihydroxybenzaldehyde substrate.

The chemically likely transformation is NaH-mediated deprotonation of a phenolic OH followed by SN2 alkylation with MOMCl, forming a phenolic O–CH2–OCH3 (MOM) ether while retaining the aldehyde. Thus the major product is a mono-MOM-protected dihydroxybenzaldehyde, not an aldehyde-reaction product.
